records.real_world_identity_notes: The observed AC EVO name maps to Alfa Romeo's 1965 Giulia Sprint 1600 GTA, the lightweight 1570 cc GTA based on the Giulia Sprint GT and developed as a road-legal basis for touring-car competition. The FIA Historic Database lists the Giulia Sprint GTA under homologation number 1395 with a 1570 cc engine and an August 2, 1965 homologation date. This is the early 1600 GTA, not the later GTA 1300 Junior, 1750/2000 GTAm, standard Giulia Sprint GT, or the modern Giulia GTA/GTAm.
records.confidence_basis: The official Alfa Romeo museum identifies the Giulia Sprint GTA and its 1570 cc, five-speed, dry single-disc clutch specification. Stellantis identifies the production model as the Giulia Sprint 1600 GTA, presented in 1965 and used as a touring-car basis. FIA records independently establish the exact Giulia Sprint GTA homologation identity and date.

records.specification_basis: The official Alfa Romeo museum lists five forward gears plus reverse, and an exact-model specification corroborates five forward speeds. The exact-model specification identifies the five-speed gearbox as fully synchronized; the official museum independently identifies the five-speed GTA transmission. The period driving impression directly calls the GTA selector a dogleg shifter. Dogleg is a manual H-gate form, while the official museum establishes the physical five-speed manual/clutch configuration.
